Mouth or genital involvement, nail damage and scalp hair loss can matter even when little skin is affected. Scalp and nail disease can cause lasting damage, so small coverage should not be treated as proof of mild disease.

psoriasis.reply:
For psoriasis: Psoriasis severity depends on more than how a patch looks. A clinician considers how much skin is affected, plaque thickness and scaling, symptoms, and the effect on everyday life. Small patches on the face, scalp, hands, feet, nails or genital skin can still have a major impact.

For a rough description of coverage, your own whole handprint, including palm, fingers and thumb together, represents about 1% of your body surface. This is only an estimate; coverage alone does not determine whether psoriasis is mild, moderate or severe.

I can help you describe these factors, but I cannot assign a clinical mild, moderate or severe grade from chat or a photo.

Which body areas are affected? Include any scalp, face, hands, feet, nails or genital involvement. You can say 'I'm not sure.'
